mechanism: Isoniazid can cause hyperuricemia and precipitate acute gout attacks, while chlorthalidone (a thiazide-like diuretic) also increases serum uric acid levels and can mask or worsen gout; additionally, both drugs may affect electrolyte balance and renal function.
action: Monitor serum uric acid levels and gout symptoms during concurrent use; consider alternative antituberculosis agents if gout develops; ensure adequate hydration and monitor electrolytes and renal function periodically.
